boards.school_name: The University of Texas at Arlington
boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Texas at Arlington, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes first-weekend loop through recognizable UTA destinations, ending with a scheduled public arts option in downtown Arlington.

cards.title: Start with the Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: First stop: campus orientation
cards.notes: Begin by locating the Welcome Center, then use its visit resources to orient yourself before setting out across the main campus.
cards.short_summary: A practical starting point for getting your bearings at UTA.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says a visitor’s adventure begins at the Dan Dipert University Welcome Center.
cards.access_notes: Check the university visit page for current visit options and campus-map links.

cards.title: Find a study base at Central Library
cards.subtitle: Second stop: a campus landmark
cards.notes: Walk to Central Library, note its location for future study sessions, and consult the library’s current hours before planning a return visit.
cards.short_summary: Put UTA’s main library on your mental map early.
cards.evidence_claim: Central Library is identified on UTA’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Hours and building access can change; verify with UTA Libraries before visiting.

cards.title: Pass through University Center
cards.subtitle: Third stop: student-center navigation
cards.notes: Use the University Center as a navigation break: look over posted campus information and identify dining or meeting spaces you may use later.
cards.short_summary: A central stop for learning the student-center layout.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Center is identified on UTA’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Food and some services may require payment; check current building information on arrival.

cards.title: Take a pause at Brazos Park
cards.subtitle: Fourth stop: outdoor campus space
cards.notes: Use this named campus green space for a brief reset, then continue your walk rather than treating the weekend as a packed itinerary.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor pause between indoor campus stops.
cards.evidence_claim: Brazos Park is identified on UTA’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and campus programming vary; follow posted university guidance.

cards.title: See what is on view at The Gallery
cards.subtitle: Fifth stop: Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Head to the first floor at the north end of the Fine Arts Building and check the gallery calendar for the exhibition currently on view.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission art stop built into the campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA states that all Gallery events are free and open to the public, and locates it in the Fine Arts Building.
cards.access_notes: Check the gallery calendar and visitor information before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Get acquainted with the MAC
cards.subtitle: Sixth stop: recreation facilities
cards.notes: Bring your Mav ID, take an introductory walk through the MAC, and ask staff which recreation spaces or equipment are available that day.
cards.short_summary: A campus-recreation stop with several activity options.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA lists fitness, courts, tracks, game-room space, and equipment checkout at the Maverick Activities Center.
cards.access_notes: UTA says equipment checkout requires a Mav ID or membership card; facility hours and activity space are subject to change.

cards.title: Locate College Park Center
cards.subtitle: Seventh stop: event venue on campus
cards.notes: Walk by College Park Center to recognize the venue, then consult its event calendar when you want to plan around a specific game or performance.
cards.short_summary: Know where a major UTA event venue sits in relation to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: College Park Center is identified on UTA’s official campus map.
cards.access_notes: Event admission, dates, and building access depend on the specific program; check its current listing.

cards.title: Plan a Planetarium show
cards.subtitle: Eighth stop: astronomy on campus
cards.notes: Check the rotating schedule, choose a show that fits your weekend, and reserve a ticket before arriving for the hour-long program.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled campus activity with science programming and a sky tour.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA says its public shows include a full-dome feature, Texas sky tour, and astronomer Q&A; each show lasts about one hour.
cards.source_title: UTA Planetarium Public Shows and Events
cards.access_notes: Public-show schedules rotate. UTA lists student public-show admission at $5; check the current schedule and ticket availability.

cards.title: Finish with a free concert, when scheduled
cards.subtitle: Ninth stop: Founders Plaza, downtown Arlington
cards.notes: If a free-concert date lines up, bring a lawn chair or blanket and check the event listing before heading to Founders Plaza.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor downtown option for a scheduled evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Levitt Pavilion Arlington’s official venue page lists free concerts and identifies the venue at 100 W. Abram St.
cards.access_notes: Attend only an event explicitly labeled free on the official calendar; listed free concerts run 7:10–10:00 p.m. on scheduled dates.

cards.title: Bookmark Maverick Stampede for the next kickoff
cards.subtitle: Tenth stop: plan a future campus event
cards.notes: Before the weekend ends, review Student Activities information and bookmark Maverick Stampede so you can join the official semester kickoff when it returns.
cards.short_summary: A documented UTA activity to watch for as the semester begins.
cards.evidence_claim: UTA identifies Maverick Stampede as the official kick-off to the new semester.
cards.access_notes: This is a recurring semester kickoff, not a guaranteed first-weekend event; check Student Activities for current dates and access details.

warnings: Campus-map publication date is represented as 2025-09-01 because the official PDF search record provides month/year but no day. Verify venue schedules and access before departure.
One source publication date is month-level in the official map record; it is normalized to 2025-09-01.
